subject: Audit logs & access evidence — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finco.com>

Cc: security@finco.com
Date: 2026-02-21T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: audit logs & PII handling (post-demo)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — appreciate the clear overview. A few follow-ups from our compliance team around audit logs and data handling:

- Can you confirm what fields are included in the audit logs (who accessed what/when)? Specifically we need user identifiers, request IDs, timestamps, resource accessed, and IPs.
- What export formats do you support (CSV/JSON/Parquet)?
- Retention: what's the default retention period for logs and can it be extended to 12+ months for compliance?
- Data residency: if we provision in eu-west, will audit logs remain in EU?
- PII handling: do logs contain raw PII or are there redaction/hashing options?

If possible, please share a sample export or schema and a short summary of controls (SOC2/Security docs). Also happy to schedule a short technical call with your security engineer.

Next steps for us: compliance will review whatever evidence you can share and decide whether we need a formal audit.

Thanks,
Alice Morgan
Director, Security & Compliance
FinCo
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, security@finco.com
Date: 2026-02-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: audit logs & PII handling (post-demo)

Hi Alice — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (high level)
- Audit log fields: we capture timestamp, request_id, caller_id (hashed by default), user_id (if provided by customer), model, route, action (create/read/delete), resource_id, tokens_in/tokens_out, response_size, and source IP.
- Export formats: CSV, JSONL, and Parquet exports are supported. We can also stream logs to your S3 or push to a customer-managed endpoint.
- Retention: default retention for hosted accounts is 90 days; we offer configurable retention up to 24 months on Dedicated/Private plans via contract.
- Data residency: logs are stored in the same region as the tenant (eu-west logs for EU tenants). For Hosted accounts we can pin region at onboarding.
- PII handling: by default we hash user identifiers and redact long textual fields in exports; we can provide tooling to strip or pseudonymize additional fields per customer policy.

Attachments I'll include: redwood_audit_log_schema.csv (schema + sample fields) and a small sample export. I'll also attach our SOC2 summary for evidence.

Proposed next steps
1) I'll share the schema and a redacted sample export by EOD today.
2) Schedule a technical call with our security engineer (Dev Patel) — would Tue/Wed next week work?
3) If you need extended retention or region guarantees, we can route to Commercial for a formal quote (I can loop in Ben Carter).

Let me know preferred time for the call and any additional evidence items your team needs.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finco.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-23T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: audit logs & PII handling (post-demo)

Hi Alice / Olga — Dev from Security/Platform here. Quick technical note and what I can provide for evidence.

Audit log delivery
- API endpoint: GET /v1/audit-logs/export (supports date range, tenant_id, and filters).
- Exports: CSV, JSONL (newline-delimited JSON), Parquet. We support direct S3 exports (customer bucket) or presigned download links (time-limited).

Fields included (sample)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (UUID)
- tenant_id
- caller_id (hashed by default; raw values can be stored if customer supplies explicit user mapping and consents)
- user_id (customer-provided)
- model_name
- route
- action
- resource_id
- tokens_in
- tokens_out
- response_hash (to allow content tracing without storing full output)
- ip_address (IPv4/IPv6)
- auth_method

PII handling & redaction
- By default we pseudonymize caller identifiers with HMAC using a tenant-scoped key. Long text fields (in rare cases when request metadata contains user-supplied names) are truncated in exports; full content is available only in logs retained under contract and only with RBAC-protected access.
- We can provide a customer-configurable export job that strips or masks additional fields prior to export.

Retention & residency
- Default retention: 90 days for Hosted accounts.
- Extended retention: available up to 24 months for Dedicated/Private (contracted feature).
- Residency: logs are stored in the same cloud region as the tenant. For EU tenants we persist in eu-west-1 and do not replicate to US by default.

Evidence we can provide
- Sample redacted export (JSONL) — attached as sample_audit_export.jsonl
- Schema CSV — attached as redwood_audit_log_schema.csv
- SOC2 summary & controls mapping (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf)
- For high-assurance audits we can generate an access report showing who accessed the export and when (signed by our internal audit process).

If you want, I can prepare an export with FinCo-specific masking rules so your team can validate. Proposed dates for a technical call: Tue 2026-02-29 10:00-11:00 PST or Wed 2026-03-01 14:00-15:00 PST.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
